lore.title: Empress of the Floating Isles
story: When the Sundering tore the western hills into the sky, a young noblewoman named Vaelora refused to let them fall. She bound the winds with a jeweled scepter and steered the broken land into the clouds, and the survivors crowned her empress of the Zephyrine Isles.

Her crystal dragon, Lirien, hatched from a gem in her crown on the day she was crowned. Her sky guard is led by Kyrielle and her storm dragon, and her court is visited each year by the dragon sovereign Draemir, whose citadel drifts at the edge of her isles.

She is elegant, merciless toward tyrants and endlessly generous toward travelers. When her isles drift over a realm at war, the fighting tends to stop, not out of fear, but because no one wants to be the one Lirien decides to dislike.

lore.title: The Starlit Librarian
story: Amethia catalogs spells the way other librarians catalog books, and she has never lost a single one. She guards the Warden Archive of Nocthaven, the library Malachar left behind, including the dangerous shelves that read their readers back.

She is the younger sister of the sorceress Nocturna, and the two have not spoken since Nocturna left the archive to serve Zarathor. Amethia sends her a letter every year anyway. None have been answered, but none have been returned either.
She is gentle, patient and very hard to anger, which makes it all the more terrifying when she finally opens one of those books in battle.

lore.title: The Clockwork Dragoon
story: As a lonely boy in Brasshelm, Dorian watched a silver storm dragon fly over the city walls with a rider on its back. He spent the next five years building a dragon of his own out of scrap and captured lightning, and named it Spark.

Now he guards the walls of Brasshelm with Spark at his side and a crackling glaive in his hands. The barons have ordered him to catch the outlaw Scarlett nine times. He has failed nine times, very carefully.
His one dream is to meet the dragon rider from his childhood. He does not know her name is Kyrielle, or that she would love to meet Spark.

lore.title: The Rune-Serpent Scholar
story: Eldric spent ten years in a windowless library in the Ironfang Highlands, translating the runes that appeared in the mountains after the Sundering. When he spoke the last word, the runes rose from the page and coiled into a serpent of blue light that has followed him ever since.
The silver in his hair came from that night. So did a terrible suspicion: the runes are the Hollow's own writing, and the same runes glow on the axe of Gorvane, the warlord who cannot die.
He follows Gorvane from battle to battle, taking notes. Gorvane tolerates him, mostly because Eldric is the only one who has ever promised to find a way for him to rest.

lore.title: The Night-Blooming Healer
story: Elowen tends the moon-flower forest of Lirael, where flowers bloom only under the moon. She knows the name of every plant, and every plant knows hers, which is why the forest grows paths for her that it hides from everyone else.
One spring night she found a baby sleeping in a nest of flowers and raised her with her sister Sylva; the baby was Verdana. Years later she took on a young herbalist, Liesel, as her apprentice.
Her golden staff carries the forest's life into battle, closing wounds and calming fears. She smiles often, and her smile is said to be the best medicine she has.

lore.title: The Wolf Without a Pack
story: Fenric was born in Hrimvald under a black moon, half man and half wolf, a child of the wind-wolf pack that lost its leader, Hrimfang, on the night of the Sundering. The pack blamed his strange birth for their bad luck and cast him out.

He went south into the Sylvaran Wilds and made the dark woods his home, learning to shoot arrows that glow with green spirit-fire. The shaman Tavik and his spirit-wolf Kesh are the closest thing to family he has.

His howl carries far on cold nights, far enough to reach the Frostgate. The knight who holds it, Boreas, carries the last of Hrimfang's strength. Fenric does not know that she has been looking for him for twenty years.

lore.title: The Blade of Falling Petals
story: Hayato trained at the Temple of a Thousand Lanterns, where students learn to cut a cherry petal in half before it touches the ground. He was the first in a century to cut it into four.

He met Kaito when both were twelve, in a duel that ended in a draw and a lifelong rivalry. His younger brother Ryuji has never been able to cut a single petal, and Hayato secretly envies him for having the courage to fight with his fists instead.
His katana carries the wind of the mountain passes, and he fights with a calm that unsettles his enemies. He believes a duel is won in the breath before the first strike.

lore.title: The Last Dragonfly
story: Kaito wears the dragonfly crest of the Tonbo clan, whose castle burned the night after the Sundering while the islands were still shaking. Masked assassins of the Kurokage, the shadow clan, did it on a rival lord's orders. Kaito, eleven years old, survived by hiding in the castle well.

He is the last swordsman of his clan, wandering the Hoshigane Isles with a blade drawn faster than the wind. His rival and closest friend, Hayato, has beaten him in exactly as many duels as he has lost to him.
Kaito hunts the Kurokage still. He does not know that the quiet fighter with blue fire in his fists, the one who has saved his life twice, was raised by them.

story: Lucan steals from nobles, lies to guards and flirts with everyone, all with the same crooked smile. His daggers trail black smoke, a gift from a shadow-imp named Grit that he won in a card game against Mortis, who claims he let him win.
He and Nyra were once the best pair of thieves in Spirehollow. She quit; he did not. He tells everyone he does not miss her. Grit, perched on his shoulder, rolls its eyes every time.
Together Lucan and Grit are the most annoying pair in the city, and the most effective.

lore.title: The Tidal Spellbreaker
story: Maren was the most brilliant student of the storm tower of Voltaris, in Cogsreach, until she discovered how easily spells could be unraveled and started unraveling her master's. Expelled, she left with her staff and a library's worth of secrets. Her friend Ophira still writes to her.

She settled on the Thalassar Coast, where the drowned temples are full of old wards that need breaking and old curses that need lifting. Isolde's Tidewatch hires her more often than either of them admits.
She fights by twisting her enemies' magic like a riptide, turning their strength against them. Few mages want to duel her twice.

lore.title: Mistress of the Violet Sigil
story: Nocturna left the Warden Archive, and her sister Amethia, to become Lord Zarathor's advisor and, for a time, much more. She left him too, the night his horned shadow spoke to her in his voice.

She leads a coven now, in a gothic chamber where candles burn with violet flame. Her sigils can silence a storm or open a door to places that should stay closed. She keeps every letter Amethia has sent her, unopened, in a locked drawer.

She is polite, amused and utterly confident. Rival sorcerers who visit her chamber often leave a little less powerful than they arrived, and Zarathor, it is said, still visits once a year, and leaves without a word.

story: Nyra hunts the thieves who hunt Spirehollow. From the rooftops she watches every alley, and her steel claws have ended the careers of more criminals than the city guard ever has.

She used to be one of them. She and Lucan were the best pair of thieves in the city until a job went wrong and a child got hurt. She quit that night; Lucan did not. They have been dancing around each other on the rooftops ever since.
She keeps a special eye on a young pickpocket named Jory, who reminds her of herself. Those she protects leave small offerings of bread on the rooftops. She always takes them.

lore.title: The Puppeteer of Tides
story: Odette's puppets dance with strings made of seawater, and her performances made her the most beloved artist of the harbor town of Merrow. Her favorite puppet, Colette, was carved from driftwood that washed ashore from Celestine's sunken temple.

Colette sometimes moves on its own, and on stormy nights it sings hymns no one in Merrow has heard in twenty years. Odette insists this is normal. Celestine, who heard it sing once, went very quiet and flew away.
In battle, the strings of Odette's magic mend her allies as gently as she repairs her dolls.

lore.title: The Ember Prodigy
story: Pyralis was six when the volcano lords burned his village, and he would have burned with it if a knight made of fire had not carried him out. He never learned the knight's name, only the legend: Ignis, guardian of the Everfire.

He set his first fire at seven and his first forest at eight. The fire mages of Emberhold took him in before he could set the whole south ablaze and taught him to shape the flame instead of feeding it. His best friend, the stone-singer Torvin, keeps the lava calm whenever Pyralis forgets to.
He is cocky, loud and genuinely brilliant. He wants to become the next guardian of the Everfire, and he has no idea Ignis has been watching him for years, wondering the same thing.

lore.title: The Raven of the Last Rites
story: Ravenna performs the last rites in the graveyard of Duskmere, guiding souls that cannot find their way. Her raven, burning with violet fire, carries the messages the dead cannot deliver themselves.

She believes Malachar's tome is a prison, and that the souls inside it deserve to move on, whatever waits beyond. Malachar believes she will feed them to the Hollow. They have argued about it for twenty years, and they are the only two people in Nocthaven who truly understand each other.
She is kind to spirits and cruel to the living who disturb them. She has told Morwen that Edric's soul is still trapped in Zarathor's shadow, and she has promised to guide it home.

story: Rosalind guards the crystal groves of the elves, where butterflies carry the forest's memories from flower to flower. Her bow is made of living crystal, and her arrows bloom on impact.
She and Faelyn trained together under the old marksman Thalion and have competed at everything since: archery, tracking, and who can annoy Thalion the most. Rosalind currently leads on the last one.
She looks delicate, and she likes it that way. Enemies who underestimate her soon find themselves tangled in roots and stung by petals sharper than steel.

lore.title: The Sun-Crowned Priestess
story: Solara was chosen as the sun's priestess on the longest day of the year, when the light crowned her in front of the whole city. A month later the Sundering broke the temple of Solmarr, and she spent her first years as priestess praying in the rubble.
A stonemason named Cassius rebuilt the temple for her, stone by stone, and the sun blessed him for it. She is the only person who can make Cassius laugh, and he is the only one who has seen her cry.
Her staff burns with the heat of noon, and her spells can turn a battlefield into a desert. She believes the sun does not hate the darkness; it simply refuses to let it win.

lore.title: The Voice of the Old Grove
story: Sylva grew up in a temple built inside a hollow tree, the oldest in the Sylvaran Wilds, where the priests taught her that every root in the world is connected. She can hear the earth breathing and heal the wounded by borrowing its strength.

Her elder sister Elowen tends the moon-flower forest; together they raised Verdana, a baby the forest itself left in a nest of flowers. Sylva is quiet and gentle, but when the grove is threatened, the roots answer her call faster than any army.
Since the Sundering the roots have been whispering something new to her: a pulse, far to the east, beating like a second heart. She is almost sure it comes from the Riftheart.

lore.title: The Golden Leaf Marksman
story: Thalion has guarded the edge of the Sylvaran Wilds for three centuries and has never let an arrow fly without purpose. His golden bow was shaped from the forest's oldest tree, which gave its branch willingly.

He trained two great archers, Faelyn and Rosalind, and lost one great friend: a human warden named Aldric who guarded the forest's edge with him for fifty years. Aldric's grandson Rowan now carries his bow, and Thalion watches over the boy without letting him know.
He is stoic, precise and fast as a gust of wind. Elven children say that if a leaf falls in Thalion's forest, he knows exactly where it landed.

lore.title: The Apprentice With a Twig
story: Albin is the apprentice of Astra, the great astrologer of the Skyspire, who took him in five years ago and has been home exactly twice since. He teaches himself from the books in her cluttered study in Greenhollow.
His wand is a twig from the garden. It works anyway, mostly. He writes Astra a report every week, which she never reads, and leaves a candle burning in the window every night in case she comes back.
His spells are small, but his heart is enormous, and his little sparks of light have mended more scraped knees than any archmage.

lore.title: The Tinker of the Brass Workshop
story: Brina can fix anything with her glowing wrench, and she can break anything even faster. Her workshop in Cogsreach is full of half-finished inventions, and about a third of them are on fire at any given moment.
She built the twin pistols of her cousin Scarlett, and every gadget the outlaw uses to escape the barons. Officially she has never met Scarlett.
She channels the steam from her machines into scalding blasts that surprise every enemy who thought she was only a mechanic.

lore.title: The Shieldbearer Who Walked Away
story: Garrick carried the shield of Gorvane, the Ironfang warlord, for fifteen years. After Gorvane's fourth death and fourth return, Garrick looked into his chieftain's eyes, did not recognize the man inside, and left.
Now he guards caravans through the mountain passes and has never lost one. He has a scar for each bandit gang that tried its luck, and he always takes the first watch around the campfire.
He still sends a coin each season to Brannoc, Gorvane's son, at the arena. Brannoc thinks it comes from his father. Garrick has never corrected him.

lore.title: The Ruin Runner
story: Kael explores the ruins the Sundering left behind, searching for treasure and trouble in equal measure. He usually finds more of the second, and sells the rest to Vexa in the night market of Spirehollow.
He is cocky, fast and good with his twin daggers. He claims he has never met a trap he could not dodge, which is why he has so many burns.
His dream is to reach the Riftheart and touch the Mystic Box. Everyone who hears this tells him he is mad. He takes it as encouragement.

lore.title: The Fox-Fire Herbalist
story: Liesel gathers herbs in the misty forests of the Sylvaran Wilds as the apprentice of the healer Elowen, and bandages any creature she finds hurt.
One of them was a fox with a tail of fire, far from its home in Cinderpeak, and it never left her side after she healed it. She named it Ember.
Ember fights fiercely for the girl who saved it, while Liesel watches from behind with her staff and a nervous smile.

lore.title: The Young Forest Warden
story: Rowan inherited his antler bow from his grandfather Aldric, the human warden who guarded the edge of the Sylvaran Wilds beside the elf Thalion for fifty years. With the bow came a promise to protect the forest.
He is young and takes the promise very seriously, maybe too seriously. He has never met Thalion, and he has no idea the elf has saved his life at least six times from a distance.
He stands between the woods and anyone who would harm them, and the forest stands behind him.

lore.title: The Iron-Fist Disciple
story: Ryuji is the younger brother of the swordsman Hayato. He could never cut a single cherry petal, so he left the Temple of a Thousand Lanterns and joined a dojo of fist fighters, to his family's horror.
He trains from dawn to dusk, punching wooden posts until his knuckles bleed. His master says he has more stubbornness than talent. Ryuji says that is the same thing.
His fists strike like a gale, and his scars prove he has never backed down from a fight. He has no idea his famous brother is proud of him.

lore.title: The Farm Boy With a Big Sword
story: Tobin found a rusty sword in his family's barn in Greenhollow and decided he was destined to be a hero. The sword is too big for him. The destiny might be too.
What Tobin does not know is that the sword is one of the twelve lost blades of the Lion Order, and that the last Lion knight, Leoric, has already come to the village twice to watch him train with it.
He is terrified of almost everything, but he never runs away. The chickens of his village, at least, consider him a legend.

lore.title: The Stone-Singer
story: Torvin grew up in the deep caverns under Cinderpeak, where the stones hum when lava flows beneath them. He learned their songs and how to make the rocks float and spin to his will.
His best friend is the fire mage Pyralis, who keeps setting things on fire, and Torvin keeps singing the lava back to sleep. They argue constantly and would die for each other.
Quiet and stubborn, he plants himself in front of his allies and lets the earth itself shield them.

lore.title: The Lantern-Street Swindler
story: Vexa runs a different scam on every street of the Spirehollow night market. She has sold the same bridge four times, and each buyer thanked her for the deal.
She buys relics from the ruin runner Kael, uses the pickpocket Jory as a lookout and has been trying to con Lucan for years, without success, because he keeps trying to con her back.
Her curved daggers come out only when the con fails, which is rare. She would rather steal your luck than your purse.
